questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4x-2y+3z=0 \\ 8x-3y+5z=9 \\ 7x-2y+4z=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 \\ 7 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =4|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(-12+10)+2(32-35)+3(-16+21) \\  & =-8-6+15 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 8 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 8 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 5 \\ -2 & -5 & 6 \\ -1 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & -5 & -6 \\ -1 & 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -5 & 4 \\ 5 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}19 \\ -49 \\ -58\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=19,y=-49,z=-58.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
questions.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+2z=1 \\ x+y+z=3 \\ y+2z=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-2(2)+2(1) \\  & =-4+2 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} \\ 4 \\ -\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=\frac{5}{2},y=4,z=-\frac{7}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
questions.problem: Consider a matrix equation $AB\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $4\times 4$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $4\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $AB\,x=d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB\,x & =d \\ {A}^{-1}AB\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x={A}^{-1}\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{4}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Given the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x-y-z=3 \\ 6x-3y-5z=5 \\ 5x-y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -13 & 9 & -16 \\ 9 & -7 & 12\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & -1 \\ 6 & -3 & -5 \\ 5 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -13 & 9 & -16 \\ 9 & -7 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=0,y=-5,z=2.$

Finally, $x+y+z=0+(-5)+2=-3.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
questions.problem:
Consider a system of $3$ linear equations in $3$ variables, written in matrix form as $A\,x=b.$ Here, $A$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $x$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $b$ is the column vector containing the constants. What are the missing parts of the derivation method shown below to find the unique solution of the system?

$$
A\,x={{field-1}}
$$

$$
{{field-2}}\,x={A}^{-1}\,b
$$

$$
{I}_{3}\,x={A}^{-1}\,{{field-3}}
$$

$$
{{field-4}}={A}^{-1}\,b
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $A\,x=b$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A\,x & =b \\ {A}^{-1}A\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,b \\ {I}_{3}\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,b \\ x & ={A}^{-1}\,b\end{aligned}
$$
